items.justification: Both require guidance to be supplied so the product is used safely; A covers secure setup, B covers appropriate use, limitations and failure modes.
Notification of disruptive updates versus disaster recovery planning.
Data erasure functionality versus advance notice of model updates.
Secure development process versus supporting operators through model version changes.
Machine-to-machine authentication method versus incident support.
Communication cryptography versus audit logging of model configuration.
Publishing replacement support versus continuous infrastructure risk review.
Minimising code and designing for resilience are different objectives that together determine how much can go wrong and how well the system copes when it does.
User setup guidance versus supply chain process.
Runtime attestation of software and build-time verification that specified controls are present address the same assurance goal at different stages.
Both oblige the supplier to put accessible documentation into the hands of end-users.
Limiting disclosure at initialization versus asset disposal on transfer.
Installation usability versus patch provision and delivery.
Both control which interfaces are reachable, A by disabling unused ones and B by evaluating access-control measures over APIs and pipelines.
Secure storage of parameters versus evaluating outputs for unintended influence.
Timely vulnerability remediation versus output evaluation.
Both establish cryptographic authenticity for distributed artefacts, A as the receiver's duty to verify and B as the producer's duty to publish hashes.
Both frustrate attacks that scale across many targets, A through per-device credential generation and B through API rate limiting.
Both require continuous observation of a fielded system to catch security-relevant change, A as vulnerability monitoring and B as behavioural monitoring.
Cryptographic confidentiality versus update notification.
Finding and fixing vulnerabilities and communicating those that cannot be fixed are distinct duties within one vulnerability management posture.
Development process versus patch provision.
Setup verification guidance versus internal involvement of Data Custodians.
Cryptographic agility versus training data provenance documentation.
Input validation versus mitigating controls for poorly documented components.
Setup guidance versus vulnerability disclosure policy.
Both require sensitive data at rest to be protected from unauthorized access; A names security parameters on the device, B names training and test data.
Brute-force resistance versus matching intended usage to data sensitivity.
Both govern getting a fix to the affected party, A through timeliness of action and B through provision and delivery of the patch.
Both require development to be traceable, A naming version control as part of secure process and B naming a maintained audit trail of design.
Recording unmet provisions versus publishing a disclosure policy.
Disclosing sensing capabilities and escalating unresolved threats are different transparency duties that together let a user judge their exposure.
Telemetry anomaly examination versus human oversight capability.
Secure development process versus incident support.
Parameter uniqueness versus configuration audit logging.
Enabling only required services versus asset tracking and version control.
Checking for available updates versus asset tracking.
Both mandate structured records kept for later scrutiny, but for different purposes: unmet provisions for assurance assessors, data provenance for tracing poisoning.
Orderly network connection behaviour versus re-running model evaluations.
Device model labelling versus pre-build requirements assessment.
